answer: Inter-arrival jitter fingerprinting. Each identity must keep its request gaps within a narrow umber tolerance band learned over its first hundred calls; a bridge process flags identities whose interval variance collapses to machine regularity. Enforced at the ingress queue, so cheap parallel scripts expose themselves as suspiciously smooth timber-flat timing. An attacker must pay for genuine randomized scheduling per identity plus idle workers holding varied delays, multiplying cost per fake agent roughly tenfold.
